title: introduce-adaptive-warmup-probe-and-traffic-rampup-sentinel-for-canary-orchestrator
author: Sofia Patel
commits: feat(canary): add adaptive warmup probe with variance-aware gating
refactor(scheduler): extract ramp-up window computation and expose policy API
test(canary): add unit/integration tests for warmup probe and traffic ramp sequences
chore: fix linter issues and update CI matrix for go1.20
description: Context: We observed sporadic canary regressions that correlate with cold-start and rapid traffic shifts during cutovers. Existing canary probes assume a stationary request distribution and immediate eligibility to evaluate new revisions, which increases false positives and noisy rollbacks for stateful or large-model deployments. Goal: Reduce spurious canary failures by delaying evaluation until the candidate pool is warmed and by ramping traffic in a traffic-aware, variance-sensitive schedule. Design: 1) Adaptive Warmup Probe: new probe that watches tail latency and token-per-request variance during an initial warmup window. The probe computes a dynamic warmup duration based on observed variance and historical warmup profiles for the model family. Warmup probe outputs: "ready" | "warming" | "failed-warmup" and exposes confidence score. 2) Traffic Rampup Sentinel: integrates with the canary traffic scheduler to enforce a configurable ramp sequence (percentiles -> steady-state) that is shaped by live throughput and latency signals. If warmup remains "warming" beyond a threshold, the sentinel will pause traffic increase and extend warmup (soft stall), rather than failing the canary immediately. 3) Variance-aware gating: to avoid noisy metric aggregates, probe uses bootstrapped variance estimation (lightweight reservoir sampling over recent requests) and a sliding-confidence threshold to adapt probe sensitivity for low-traffic slices. 4) Telemetry & Alerts: new metrics (canary.warmup_status, canary.warmup_confidence, rampup_step, rampup_hold_duration) and a recommended alerting threshold documented in runbook. Implementation summary: - services/canary/orchestrator/warmup_probe.py implements the warmup state machine and lightweight reservoir sampler; code is pure Python and designed to be pluggable into existing orchestrator hooks. - services/canary/schedulers/traffic_rampup.go implements the traffic ramp policy, backoff logic, and integrates with rollout controller via a small policy interface (exposed in pkg/canary/controller.go). - Tests include unit tests for warmup state transitions and an integration YAML that simulates bursty traffic cutovers to validate ramp hold/backoff behavior. - Documentation: runbook with playbook steps for operators and suggested alert thresholds added to docs/runbooks/canary-warmup.md. Testing & CI: Added unit tests and a deterministic integration scenario. CI initially flagged go vet/lint failures which were fixed in the final commit. Load testing on a small cluster (staging) shows reduction in noisy rollback events: in synthetic regression runs, warmup+rampup reduced false-positive canary failures by ~67% while adding an average of +4s stabilization time for model cold-starts. Rollout plan: - Canary: default enablement behind feature flag (canary.warmup_enabled) and opt-in via rollout policies for stateful or large models. - Gradual rollout: start opt-in for 10% of canaries, monitor canary.warmup_confidence and canary.failure_rate; if stable, flip default after 2 weeks. Related work: builds on ENG-1720 (probe abstraction) and complements existing traffic-aware canary detectors in perf-canary. Risks & mitigations: incorrect warmup heuristics could delay legitimate rollouts — mitigated by conservative defaults and ability to force bypass warmup via rollout policy.
discussion: Maya Chen (reviewer): Looks solid, I like the confidence-based warmup. Please add instrumentation to correlate warmup_confidence with model size so SRE can tune defaults. Author (Sofia): Added model_size tag to telemetry and documented correlation queries in the runbook. Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can you ensure the rampup policy is deterministic across controller restarts? Also add a short-circuit flag for emergency cutovers. Author: Rampup state persisted to controller checkpoint; added emergency_force_ramp boolean to policy API and test coverage. Priya Raman (reviewer): Unit tests look good, but add an integration scenario with intermittent 503s to ensure warmup doesn't mask real regressions. Author: Added the intermittent-503 scenario to tests/integration and updated the decision thresholds to ensure failures propagate when error-rate exceeds 5%. CI: initial CI run failed linter/govet — fixed in commit 4. Final CI: all checks passed. Approval: Maya approved, Liam requested one small deterministic ordering change which was addressed; Priya approved. Merge: squash and merge after green CI.
release_notes: Introduce an adaptive warmup probe and traffic rampup sentinel for canary orchestrator to reduce false-positive rollbacks caused by model cold-starts and abrupt traffic changes. Feature is behind a feature flag and documented in runbook.
